system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

tools.description: Read one workspace file. Lines are numbered.
tools.name: read_file

path.description: File name inside the workspace, e.g. inventory.py

tools.description: List the files in the audit workspace.
tools.name: list_files

parts.text:
Audit step 1: Enumerate the inventory-service workspace recursively and list every file it contains (source, tests, config, build and dependency manifests), so the audit scope is complete.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 1, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "average_daily_sales divides by len(sales), which raises ZeroDivisionError when sales is an empty list."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "range(1, len(items)) starts at index 1, so the first item is never checked and low_stock misses it."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file opened here is never closed (no with block or close call), so the handle leaks and written data may not be flushed."}]}

Audit step 2: Audit the source files for logic defects such as off-by-one errors, wrong stock or quantity arithmetic, unchecked null or missing values, and incorrect comparisons, recording the file and line number for each.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 2, "files": ["inventory.py", "report.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "average_daily_sales divides by len(sales) without checking for an empty list, so missing sales data raises ZeroDivisionError."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "Off-by-one: range(1, len(items)) starts at index 1, so the first item is never compared against the threshold and low_stock can miss it."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file handle from open() is never closed (no with block or close call), so buffered summary rows may not be flushed to disk."}]}

Audit step 3: Audit the config, dependency and input-handling files for security and robustness defects such as hardcoded secrets, unvalidated input, injection risks, swallowed errors and missing error handling, recording the file and line number for each.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 3, "files": ["report.py", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The caller-supplied path is opened for writing with no validation and no error handling, so an untrusted path can overwrite any writable file and a bad path raises an unhandled exception."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 7, "explanation": "row['sku'] and row['stock'] are read without checking the keys exist, so one malformed row raises KeyError partway through and leaves a partial, unclosed output file."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "The sales input is not validated, so an empty list causes an unhandled ZeroDivisionError, and a non-numeric entry would already have failed at line 7."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 22, "explanation": "items[i][\"stock\"] and items[i][\"sku\"] are accessed without checking the keys exist or that stock is numeric, so malformed input raises an unhandled KeyError or TypeError."}]}

Audit step 4: Re-read every file flagged in the previous steps to confirm each defect, then report each one with its file, line number and a one-sentence explanation.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.
